record.paper_title: Selected open problems in Matching Under Preferences
record.context_brief: robust stable matchings in stable roommates
record.original_question: Develop a theory of robust stable matchings for the Stable Roommates problem, including definitions, existence questions, and algorithms, under robustness notions analogous to those already studied for stable marriage and stable marriage with incomplete lists.

evidence.quote: As far as we are aware, robust stable matchings in sr have not been studied previously (either in the senses of Mai and Vazirani [66, 67] or Chen et al. [26]).

artifact.self_contained_problem:
The Stable Roommates problem (SR) is defined as follows. Let A be a set of 2n agents. Each agent a ∈ A submits a strict linear preference ordering over A \ {a}. A matching M is a partition of A into n unordered pairs. A pair {x, y} ∉ M is a blocking pair for M if x prefers y to its partner in M and y prefers x to its partner in M. A matching M is stable if it admits no blocking pair. (Unlike the bipartite Stable Marriage problem, an SR instance need not admit any stable matching.)

For the Stable Marriage problem (with or without incomplete lists), several notions of "robust" stable matchings have been studied. Two representative notions are:

(i) Robustness to input errors (Mai–Vazirani style): Given an SM instance I together with a discrete probability distribution over a specified polynomial-size family of perturbed instances obtained from I by simple modifications of the preference lists, find a stable matching M of I that maximizes the probability that M remains stable in a perturbed instance drawn from the distribution.

(ii) Robustness via d-robust stability (Chen et al. style): Given an SM instance I and a non-negative integer d, a stable matching M of I is called d-robust if, after any adversarial perturbation of the preferences of bounded magnitude d (e.g. each preference list is swapped at most d times), one can repair M into a stable matching of the perturbed instance by a bounded amount of modification; equivalently, M remains "close" to a stable matching under all admissible perturbations.

Develop an analogous theory of robust stable matchings for the Stable Roommates problem (with complete or incomplete preference lists). Specifically:

(a) Formulate appropriate definitions of robust stable matchings for SR under perturbation models analogous to (i) and (ii) above, taking into account that an SR instance may have no stable matching at all.

(b) Determine for which SR instances robust stable matchings (under each definition) are guaranteed to exist, and characterize them structurally.

(c) Design algorithms (or establish hardness results) for deciding the existence of, and for computing, robust stable matchings in SR instances under these definitions.
artifact.status_search_result: A web search shows that robust stable matchings have been studied for bipartite Stable Marriage (e.g., Mai–Vazirani, Chen et al.), and that recent (2023–2024) work on the Stable Roommates problem has addressed related but distinct topics such as almost-stable matchings, stability against robust deviations, manipulation, preference modification to enforce stability, and "good-enough" matchings. No source was found that develops a full theory of robust stable matchings for SR in the senses analogous to Mai–Vazirani or Chen et al., so the program appears to remain open.

status_evidence.title: Stability against robust deviations in the roommate problem
status_evidence.snippet: Proposes a solution concept weakening stability in the roommate problem via robust deviations up to depth k.
status_evidence.claim: A related but different robustness notion (SaRD) has been introduced for SR, distinct from the Mai–Vazirani / Chen et al. perturbation-based robustness for SM.

status_evidence.title: Finding Stable Matchings That Are Robust to Errors in the Input (ESA 2018)
status_evidence.snippet: Mai and Vazirani study robust stable matchings under input perturbations for the Stable Marriage problem.
status_evidence.claim: The original Mai–Vazirani robustness framework is for Stable Marriage, not Stable Roommates.

status_evidence.title: Manipulating the outcome of stable matching and roommates problems
status_evidence.snippet: Studies preference modification and manipulation for SR; shows NP-completeness for several variants.
status_evidence.claim: Recent SR research addresses preference modification and manipulation, not the requested robust-stable-matching theory.
